findings.title: Golden-capture success check is self-contradictory as written
findings.description: Task 2.2 says to "Remove the write step before committing" and then "Run the test twice. **Success:** both runs pass, and `git status` shows the golden files unchanged after the second run." Once the write step is removed, the test only compares against goldens; it can no longer capture or rewrite them, so "the golden files unchanged after the second run" is a static condition rather than evidence of determinism, and the text does not tell the executor at which point to remove the write step relative to the two runs. A junior could either capture, remove the step, then run twice (the intended reading), or try to run twice with the write step still present and destroy the just-captured goldens. Reorder the steps explicitly: capture once with the write step → remove the write step → run twice and check `git status`. The same pattern appears in 5.1 ("confirm the snapshot assertion fails, then revert"), where the expected-failure outcome should also be a named success condition rather than an unstated one.
